answer.rationale: p99 latency spike began 90 minutes ago, 2 hours after a release; this temporal coupling strongly suggests the release is the root cause. memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback is our fastest path to clearing a write-path error spike without customer impact. memory_b4 validates that we have reliable fallback patterns. We cannot add capacity fast enough during peak settlement traffic, regional failover doesn't address a bad build, and routing read queries doesn't help writes on the critical path. Rollback restores the prior stable build (memory_b1 precedent) and preserves write safety during the heaviest traffic window. This is a single, high-confidence intervention that directly addresses the timing signature of the incident.
